claims: Issue #664 reports s(271) <= 16.948947733714, the exact rational side of search/packer/candidates/s271_ex1.cert rounded up at 12 places, 4.46e-5 below 16.948992356451 (Francisco Couzo #561, refining Nate Chaoweeraprasit's SQUISH packing #500; also #586, #593); it prints the certificate side 16.948947733713657510723401112423 with the SHA-256 of s271_ex1.cert and of s271_ex1_regularized.cert, the same packing regularized for display at the same side with 21 angle groups.

Both of the source's exact rational checkers, search/exact/verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), standard library only, accept both files; the issue says they share an author and the certificate format.

The issue calls it a refinement of the #561 packing, not a new construction, and a different local minimum, by numerical evidence at 80 digits, not interval proofs: its load-bearing tilt angles match #561's group for group within 0.12 degrees, except that #561's four squares near 31.7 to 32.0 degrees are three here (67 load-bearing tilted squares against 68); KKT, strict modulo 54 exact flat motions against #561's 56, no corner-corner MILP descent, 116 + 1488 contact equations, 259 corner-corner contacts, 4 rattlers and 69 tilted squares; matched by optimal assignment over the eight box symmetries, 59 load-bearing squares move by more than 1e-4 and 2 by more than 1e-2 (at most 0.391).

The issue says the packing came from the author's basin explorer (search/packer/explore.py, fixed-side perturbation moves and re-polish) started from the register's witness at 271 as one of 52 counts in a test run: one move swapped the tilt angles of two neighbouring squares 90 seconds in, and exactsolve.py certified the point; it asks that Francisco Couzo's #561 packing and Nate Chaoweeraprasit's SQUISH packing it refines be credited.
No closed form, no interval proof of local optimality and no optimality claim.
